# claude-statusline

> A fast, dependency-light Rust status line for Claude Code. It renders the JSON Claude Code streams on stdin as a single powerline row — model, git branch, color-coded context-window usage, live cost (session, per-hour burn rate, and today's total across all sessions), chronis task, rate limits, and lines changed — and never blanks, hangs, or panics.

claude-statusline is installed with `cargo install --git https://github.com/decebal/claude-statusline` and wired via the `statusLine.command` key in `~/.claude/settings.json`. It is MIT-licensed and depends only on `serde` and `serde_json`.

## Key facts
- Language: Rust, single stripped binary (~470 KB), two dependencies (serde, serde_json).
- Segments: model, repo/dir, git branch (read from `.git/HEAD`, no subprocess), context % (green <50 / yellow 50–80 / bold-red >80 or `exceeds_200k_tokens`), cost cluster (`session · ~$/hr burn · today $total`), chronis task, rate limits (5h/7d, Pro/Max), lines ±.
- Cost: session cost and burn rate come from stdin; today's total is computed from token `usage` in `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` × a per-model price table because transcripts store `costUSD: null`. Cache rates follow Anthropic ratios (read 0.10×, 5-min write 1.25×, 1-hour write 2.0×). Override prices via `~/.claude/statusline-pricing.json`.
- Agent health: an optional first segment (rules/truth/task/stability + green-yellow-red verdict) read from `~/.claude/agent-health/<session_id>.json`. Two bundled hooks fill it — `claude-health-hook` (PostToolUse + PostToolUseFailure) writes the observable stability + drift; `claude-health-report` (Stop) grades rules/truth/task with a cheap judge model (~$0.02/turn, detached so it never blocks the turn, guarded against recursing into itself). Unscored dimensions render `–`; nothing is ever invented.
- Guarantees: always prints one non-empty line and exits 0 on any input (verified across ~40 malformed/hostile inputs); `cn` lookup bounded to ≤800 ms and cached per-cwd; daily scan cached 60 s; warm renders single-digit milliseconds.
- Responsive width: reads `COLUMNS` (Claude Code v2.1.153+) and degrades gracefully on narrow/split screens — drops lines± → rate limit → cost burn/today extras → repo → git branch → task, always keeping the essentials (model, context %, cost). Unset COLUMNS = full render.
- Config env vars: `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ASCII=1` (ASCII fallback, no Nerd Font), `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_NO_DAILY=1` (skip transcript scan), `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_CN_TTL` (task cache TTL, default 8s), `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_CN_BIN` (path to cn).

## Docs
- [README](README.md): install, configuration, cost model, comparison, and FAQ.
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): MIT.

## FAQ
- Does it need a Nerd Font? No — `CLAUDE_STATUSLINE_ASCII=1` renders plain-text labels with colors.
- How is today's cost computed? Sum of today's transcript token usage × per-model pricing (transcripts store no per-line cost).
- Will it slow Claude Code down? No — single-digit-ms warm renders, the one external call (`cn`) is capped and cached, no git/jq subprocess on the hot path.
- Does it require chronis? No — the task segment is omitted if `cn` or a task is absent.
- What on malformed input? It still prints a valid line and exits 0; only the affected segment is omitted.
